key_insight: CLIN-SUMM reduced clinical-note word count by 75% while creating reusable longitudinal summaries that improved dementia risk prediction over raw notes.
clinical_relevance: Structured, time-aware summaries could make lengthy patient histories easier to review and support longitudinal research and prediction.
method: Incrementally summarize newly documented information at each encounter without accessing future data.
Organize patient information into structured categories and date partitions.
Fine-tune Clinical ModernBERT on summaries and combine predictions with structured EHR variables.
evidence_signal: Across 12,356 Massachusetts General Hospital patients, summaries had high clinician-rated correctness and completeness; 3-year dementia prediction AUROC was 0.66 versus 0.63 with raw notes, rising to 0.69 with structured EHR variables.
watch_item: The abstract reports a single-institution evaluation; generalizability and prospective clinical utility remain to be established.
paper_title: CLIN-SUMM: Incremental Longitudinal Summarization of Clinical Notes Enables Scalable Representation and Early Disease Prediction
